attempts.summary: Brought node1's lan-b-facing interface (vtnet2, MAC-matched to node3's eth1 via live traffic capture) into service as a new OPNsense zone "optb" at 10.60.1.1/24, with a matching default-allow firewall rule. Gave node3's eth1 a persistent static IP (10.60.1.12/24) and a persistent host route so node3 reaches node2 on the existing lan (lan-a, 10.100.203.0/24) routed through node1 — proven via TTL decrement and simultaneous tcpdump on both of node1's interfaces showing the packet enter on lan-b and exit NAT'd toward node2 on lan. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol: node1's FreeBSD reboot succeeded on the first try (kern.boottime changed); node2/node3's first reboot attempts silently failed (nohup lost PATH to `shutdown`), corrected to `sudo /sbin/shutdown -r now`, after which both genuinely rebooted (new `last reboot`/`who -r` entries superseding the original Aug-26 boot). All zone config, NAT, firewall rules, static IP, and the persistent route survived every restart, and end-to-end connectivity (node3→node1 lan-b, node3→node2 via node1) was reverified healthy after the final restart.
